_comment: Mutation testing over the modules where a surviving mutant means silent divergence rather than a visible bug. Coverage proves a line ran; this proves something checked what it did. Scoped rather than repo-wide because triage is the real cost, and a mutant in a dev warning is not worth anyone's afternoon.
vitest_comment: `related` off. The runner defaults it on: for every mutant it hands Vitest the test files `perTest` coverage selected, then asks Vitest to prune that list to the ones its module graph calls related to the mutated file. The pruning is not reproducible — it reads a Vite module graph whose contents depend on what the process has already transformed — and when it prunes too hard the mutant runs almost no tests and is reported Survived. That is a false survivor: the suite does kill it, Vitest was never asked to run it. It cost this repo eight straight scheduled failures (2026-10-11 to 10-28), the score falling 93.03 -> 13.59 -> 0.72 as the pruning got more aggressive, on a tree with no commit and no dependency change — `clock.ts` scored 0.00 in CI and 97.14 locally on the same commit. With it off, Stryker's own `perTest` filter decides which tests run, which is the thing we actually want to measure.
plugins_comment: Named explicitly: pnpm's strict node_modules means Stryker's auto-discovery walks a tree the plugin is not hoisted into.
thresholds_comment: break is the roadmap's target, now met, and it applies to the overall score. Every individual module is also >=90 (see MUTATION.md); Stryker cannot gate per file, so that part is a review target. Ratchet this up as survivors die — never down.
